title: Measuring stigma for key populations: Protocol for a systematic review
author: Alanna Fitzgerald-Husek
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ka6cshe

steps.title: Execute Electronic Database Searches
steps.instruction: Perform searches across six databases (PsycINFO, PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL Plus, Global Health, and WHO Global Health Library) using the developed Boolean search strategies combining key population concepts and stigma concepts.

substeps.instruction: Apply the specific search strings for each database as detailed in Appendix 1.
Use a combination of free text words, title/abstract searches, and controlled vocabulary (e.g., MeSH, descriptor terms, Emtree).

steps.title: Identify Additional Studies via Manual Search
steps.instruction: Supplement electronic searches by manually searching citation lists of included studies and performing forward searching to identify relevant articles that referenced the included studies.

steps.title: Manage and Filter Initial Results
steps.instruction: Import all search results into EndNote (version X5) and refine the dataset.

substeps.instruction: De-duplicate references, prioritizing the order: PsycINFO, PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL Plus, Global Health, and WHO Global Health Library.
Apply a date filter (either 1 January 2000 or 1 January 2004 onwards).
Remove non-article and non-theses entries (e.g., book chapters, editorials).
Export remaining entries into an Excel spreadsheet for screening.

steps.title: Perform First Title and Abstract Screening
steps.instruction: Conduct an independent review of all titles and abstracts by two reviewers (AFH and either MVW or CH) to assess eligibility based on the measurement concept.

substeps.instruction: Complete a pilot screen of 100 entries to ensure inter-reviewer agreement.
Perform periodic spot-checks for consistency.
Resolve discrepancies through discussion; if no consensus is reached, include the entry for a second screening.
Retrieve abstracts for any entries missing them unless the title is obviously inappropriate.

steps.title: Perform Second Title and Abstract Screening
steps.instruction: Conduct a second dual-reviewer screening of studies passing the first round, focusing specifically on whether the study measures SW- or MSM-associated stigma using a metric, scale, or similar construct.

substeps.instruction: Exclude studies that do not identify measurement methods or use indirect/proxy measures.
Resolve discrepancies via discussion or consultation with the systematic review supervisor (SB).

steps.title: Conduct Full-Text Review
steps.instruction: Independently review the full-text PDFs of studies that passed abstract screening to confirm they meet all eligibility criteria, specifically the use of identified metrics or scales.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve PDFs via EndNote or manual search.
Track inclusion/exclusion in Excel spreadsheets.
Resolve discrepancies using the same process as the second abstract screening.
Use column hiding in Excel to avoid reviewer bias.

steps.title: Abstract Data from Included Studies
steps.instruction: Extract data from all included studies using the standardized abstraction form (Appendix 4), with one author extracting and a second independent reviewer verifying.

substeps.instruction: Perform a pilot abstraction on one quantitative, one qualitative, and one mixed-methods article.
Extract information across three categories: study characteristics (design, quality), population (study and target populations), and stigma (type, domain, level, metric).
Contact study authors for missing or unclear information where possible.

steps.title: Assess Methodological Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality and risk of bias of included studies, with one author extracting data and another verifying.

substeps.instruction: For quantitative and mixed-methods studies: Use the modified Downs and Black checklist (max score 22, cut-off of 11 for high quality), excluding items 8, 14, 15, 17, and 27.
For qualitative studies: Use the Spencer et al. quality framework (18 questions, cut-off score > 9 for high quality).

steps.title: Synthesize and Analyze Results
steps.instruction: Summarize the abstracted data and perform qualitative and basic quantitative analyses.

substeps.instruction: Create a PRISMA flow diagram of study selection.
Develop a comparison chart of features (e.g., validated stigma scales).
Conduct subgroup qualitative analyses by stigma type, domain, level, population, or definition of practices.
Perform simple quantitative calculations (e.g., proportion of studies measuring SW-associated stigma).
Handle missing data by contacting authors or performing sensitivity analyses (including vs. excluding studies); consider conservative imputation.
